findings.summary: H5 makes the gate's capability set 'None' (Q-HE2S-9 (a)). Four adopted data contracts still let the gate hold CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE with a signed port below 1024, and HS43 records none of them. They are not in the closed list, not carried as obligations, and not mentioned in notAmended. notAmended in fact keeps 'SELinux matrix v4's matrix.json' as unchanged. These are silent supersessions introduced by H5.
findings.evidence: architecture/native-profile-v3/qualification.schema.json, $defs/roles/properties/EFFECT_GATE/capabilities: enum [[], ["CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE"]]. scripts/native_qualification_v3.py:327-328: 'CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE only for a signed port below 1024'. architecture/native-profile-v2/README.md:77: 'CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE only with a signed port below 1024'. Both native-profile contracts are ADOPTED_DATA_CONTRACT. architecture/selinux-matrix-v2/matrix.json:1394 (A48) and selinux-matrix/matrix.json:1394: 'CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE only for systemd, the server and gate (enrolled only with a signed port below 1024), ...'. Both matrices grant planeon_gate_t 'capability net_bind_service'; README A45-A48 (v4:220, v3:184) list the gate. Scenario: a qualification record with EFFECT_GATE capabilities [CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE] and a signed I04 port of 443 passes native-profile v3 but breaks W01 §5.3 as amended by H5. The broker's read of the gate's exe link then fails (the gate's permitted set is outside the broker's), so the broker never connects. This fails closed, but the contracts disagree. Required: carry these as obligations for their successors (the queued matrix amendment SELINUX-MATRIX-I04-KEYCERT: drop the gate from A48 and its grant; the native-profile successor: EFFECT_GATE capabilities [[]]), or add the text clauses to the closed list. H5 is still pending the monitor; if H5 is dropped, say in §12 that Q-HE2S-9 forecloses the branch instead.

findings.summary: O-W03-WRITER-EXE's only concrete mechanism, 'SECBIT_NOROOT and an empty bounding set in the starter', cannot be carried out by the starter. Both steps need CAP_SETPCAP, and planeon_admin_t, the only domain that may start the writer, does not hold it in matrix v4.
findings.evidence: Linux v6.12, from my own knowledge: PR_SET_SECUREBITS (cap_task_prctl) and PR_CAPBSET_DROP (cap_prctl_drop) both return EPERM without CAP_SETPCAP, and SELinux then checks 'capability setpcap' for the caller. matrix.json: EXECUTE on planeon_policy_writer_exec_t belongs only to planeon_admin_t. planeon_admin_t's capabilities are closed: chown, dac_override, fowner, fsetid, kill, setgid, setuid, net_bind_service, sys_boot, sys_nice, sys_resource, audit_write (no setpcap; README decision 6). A route that works: a root starter whose permitted set covers its bounding set (an ordinary root login). Its exec gives permitted = bounding (cap_bprm_creds_from_file), which is a subset of the starter's, so commit_creds keeps the writer dumpable. The writer then empties its own sets with capset before it installs its filter. Dropping needs no capability, but it does need SELinux 'process setcap' for planeon_policy_writer_t, which matrix v4 does not model, and the writer's filter has no capset. Required: replace the example with that route, or name a starter that holds setpcap.

findings.summary: The two procAccess obligations imply SELinux can narrow the gated entries alone. It cannot: gated and ungated /proc entries carry the same label and are checked with the same permission.
findings.evidence: From my own knowledge of v6.12. Every /proc/<pid> inode takes the task's SID (selinux_task_to_inode). The ptrace-read LSM check is 'file read' on that SID (selinux_ptrace_access_check), the same permission a read of stat, status or cgroup needs. environ and maps are class file, like stat and status, so dropping them through procAccess also drops the captures' ungated reads. Only class lnk_file (exe, cwd, root, fd/*) separates. Native-profile v3 P1 also records every role's /proc/<pid>/exe (README:60), so whoever captures the gate needs its exe link, not only the broker. The evaluation should state these limits. 'Evaluate' leaves room for it, so this is not a defect of the obligation.
